title: The Brainlets of YT Fitness don't understand Science
summary: Part 2 of NH's series on science in YouTube fitness, aimed at the anti-science meathead camp (often enhanced current or former pro bodybuilders). He says they focus on cardio, diet and exercise variety, reject programming and RPE, spread low natural limits, market a dominating father figure to young fans and push PEDs. He argues for a middle ground where science means applied, empirical programming, with mind and body developed together.
claims: YouTube fitness swings like a pendulum between a science camp and an anti-science camp; meatheads on steroids came first, then smaller science-based lifters, and now an anti-science wave is back
Anti-science fitness YouTubers are typically current or former pro bodybuilders, from openly enhanced to TRT-level users to those claiming natural
Their content centres on cardio, diet and exercise selection, none of which drives growth for naturals the way programming does
Endless exercise variation slows growth because you constantly cycle lifts and never progress; it appeals to people who hate routine, and novices grow anyway until they stall hard
For NH science means empiricism: applied practices and programming; he is neither pro nor anti science because it is not his god
Science on YouTube fitness has skewed toward the mental side, with PhDs who look like they do not lift, which the muscular anti-intellectuals exploit
You need both mind and body; you are a spirit within a body, and when one stalls the other stalls too
Genetically gifted lifters who grew doing anything wrongly tell everyone to just move their body and lift, which does not work for people who struggle to grow
Delusional gym-goers who have lifted 15 years without looking it, with invisible lat syndrome and maxing the cable stack, have neither results nor knowledge
PED users should not tell anyone they do not need science or programming, since drugs got them big
Progress in bodybuilding depends on will and on learning to program; once you decide you are done learning, you are also done growing
Telling people they hit their natural limit after two years of training is idiotic; ten years ago even the most pessimistic YouTubers said five years, so the claimed limit keeps shrinking
Being proud of being stupid is not masculinity; being a man means becoming sophisticated, and big biceps are only part of it
Paralysis by analysis means focusing on theory over practice, not that programming is useless; lifting is proactive and you have to actually do it
Saying RPE does not work means saying intensity does not work; every set falls somewhere on the intensity scale whether you log it or not
NH prefers percentages to RPE for bodybuilding, but intensity is key either way
If a channel you learn from never talks volume, intensity and frequency, drop it
Diet matters less than people think for naturals: once macros are set, it stays fairly stable for life
NH does not do cardio; it is not necessary to be lean
Biomechanics gurus' tweaks like angling the arm 30 degrees on a curl are things you learn yourself by lifting, and another person's body is not yours
Drama sells on YouTube fitness, so neither camp wants the pendulum to stop
Replacing trust in science with trust me bro from a big PED user means trusting someone who is big because of drugs
Relativism lets fitness influencers dodge any argument because they do not really hold positions
Disregard any title promising results in less than a month; even novices cannot get big arms in two weeks, and advanced progress takes years
Promising fast results promotes PED use, body dysmorphia and frustration
The big-brother style of fitness YouTuber is fine and is how NH got into lifting; the insulting daddy-talk style is exploitative
Young men lacking a father figure seek hyper-masculine YouTubers and put themselves in a submissive position that gets exploited to sell products
Fanatical fanboy cults around a YouTuber kill the truth; NH wants his commenters to keep shutting down sycophants
Anti-science influencers stall, take PEDs, and tell followers to train two years then do steroids, which is morally reprehensible; there is never a good time to take drugs
Being bigger is not an argument; a 160 lb person can know more about nutrition than a big lifter
Being smart is no excuse for not training, and being athletic is no excuse for not learning; do both
Everyone follows a program even if training by instinct; write down exercises, sets, volume, intensity and frequency and that is a program, you just do not know what you are doing
Like a tennis player who studies the sport, a bodybuilder has to be a student of the game while still lifting
Once you have learned to build a big body naturally you can help others; PED users who got big do not pass down knowledge
